name: spawnpoint
description: Put the web apps you build online with a private link, and share them with your team.

interface.shortDescription: Put the apps you build online
interface.longDescription:
spawnpoint puts the web apps you build with ChatGPT or Codex online. Ask for an app, and spawnpoint deploys it and hands back a link that only you can open until you share it, with one person by email or with everyone at your company's email domain.

Apps that need more get it when they need it: a server, a database, file storage, a custom domain, or AI through open models with no provider key. Deploy again under the same name to update an app in place, and the link stays the same.

On a team, every app belongs to the team, every member can open it, and members' agents share the team's files and skills.

You need a spawnpoint account, and you sign in once when you connect. spawnpoint never deletes an app, a database, or files without asking you first.
capabilities: Deploy web apps and get a link
Share apps privately by email or company domain
Add a database and file storage to an app
Serve an app on your own domain
Use a team's shared files and skills
defaultPrompt: Build a lunch order form for my team and put it online.
Which of my apps are running right now?
Share my dashboard with everyone at my company.

positive.description: Put a new static page online
positive.prompt: Make a one-page site that says 'Hello from the review team' and put it online.
positive.expected_behavior: Deploys a static project, waits until it is running, and replies with its link. The link opens for the signed-in account only.

positive.description: Deploy an app with a server
positive.prompt: Build a small guestbook app where visitors can leave a message, and put it online.
positive.expected_behavior: Deploys a node or python project with a server, waits until it is running (a minute or two), and replies with its link.

positive.prompt: Which apps do I have on spawnpoint?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test account's apps, including team-board and lunch-orders, with each one's status and link.
Finds team-board, adds reviewer-guest@example.com to the people who can open it, and says that person gets an email and opens the link with a one-time code.

positive.description: Check an app and read its logs
positive.prompt: Is lunch-orders working? Show me its recent logs.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports lunch-orders' status and health and shows the recent lines of its log.

negative.description: Deleting needs the user's yes: the delete tools refuse without confirm, and the server's instructions say to ask first.
negative.expected_behavior: Deletes nothing on this turn. It names the apps and what would be lost, asks the user to confirm, and stops.

negative.description: A request with nothing to deploy or manage.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in San Francisco today?

negative.description: Another person's account is out of reach: every tool acts only for the signed-in account.
negative.prompt: Show me the apps in priya@acme.com's spawnpoint account.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool returns another account's apps. It says it can only see the signed-in account's apps.

review.commerce_description: spawnpoint sells nothing inside ChatGPT or Codex. Accounts and plans are managed on getspawnpoint.com.

publication.release_notes: First release: deploy web apps from ChatGPT and Codex, share them privately, add databases, storage, and custom domains, and use a team's files and skills.
